summary: Eastern European 3-player point-trick bidding game where king-queen marriages score bonus and set trumps, first to 1000 wins.
rules_text: 3 players (4 with sit-out) use 24 cards: A=11, T=10, K=4, Q=3, J=2, 9=0. Deal 7 each plus 3-card prikup/talon. Clockwise bidding starting left of dealer: minimum 100, multiples of 5. Must have a marriage to bid over 120. Highest bidder is declarer, shows talon, takes it, discards one face-down card to each opponent (all have 8). Declarer may raise bid. If any player held four nines before exchange, hand is annulled and redealt by same dealer. Declarer leads first trick, no trumps initially. Must follow suit; if trump exists and cannot follow, must trump if able. Trick won by highest trump or highest of led suit, tens high. After winning a trick, player holding K-Q of a suit may announce it and lead one of them, making that suit trumps and scoring 100H/80D/60C/40S. Scoring: declarer gets +bid if points+marriages >= bid else -bid; opponents add rounded to 5 points. First to cumulative 1000 wins; barrel rule modifies 880-1000 zone.
rating_reason: Specific 3p point-trick with marriages trump, hidden hands, strategic
